body.statement: Theorem 2 (sound partial certificate procedure).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the two output formats of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) are mutually exclusive and sound.  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and \(y\), the equality branch returns \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with finite identities and \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for all \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), \(D\), and \(y\).  If some normal form is nonzero, its bounded rational enumeration contains at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) candidate tables and returns a separator if and only if such a candidate of coordinate bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) exists; every returned separator certifies unequal graphwise intervention vectors.  Thus the equality branch implies a common intervention law, but unconditional termination of the nonzero branch and the converse from a common law to the equality branch are not asserted.
body.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an effect-complete common-functional-or-counterexample contract.
body.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo prove only a sufficient simultaneous criterion; Perkovic is complete for one MPDAG rather than a tied family across MECs.
body.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit or an exact ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\).  First suppose that every normal form is zero.  The finite identities supplied by the narrowed certificate lemma have, for each \((D,y)\), the form
\[
 s^{N_{D,y}}\left(F_{D,y}^{2k_{D,y}}+
       \sum_iq_{D,y,i}^2\right)=\sum_j a_{D,y,j}f_j,
 \qquad J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle .
\]
Let \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  The oracle-one and normalization conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) give \(f_j(p)=0\) for every \(j\).  Strict positivity gives \(p_z>0\).  Every recorded denominator is a product of observed marginal probabilities, each of which is a nonempty sum of positive cells; hence \(B_{D,y}(p)>0\) for every \((D,y)\), and therefore \(s(p)\neq0\).  Evaluating the certificate and dividing by \(s(p)^{N_{D,y}}\) yields
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)^{2k_{D,y}}+\sum_iq_{D,y,i}(p)^2=0.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative, so \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  By the cross-signature definition and positivity of both denominators,
\[
 0=A_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)-A_{D_0,y}(p)B_{D,y}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p).
\]
This holds for every \(D,y,p\), proving soundness of the equality circuit and its common-law conclusion.

For the second branch, an integer of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) has fewer than \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) signed possibilities.  A reduced rational coordinate therefore has fewer than \(2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) numerator--denominator descriptions.  Taking \(m\) coordinates gives fewer than
\[
 2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
descriptions, before positivity, normalization, or coprimality removes any of them.  Canonical finite enumeration consequently checks no more than this number of distinct candidates.  Exact checks of positivity, normalization, oracle-one equations, every oracle-zero sum of squares, and a failed signature decide whether a candidate belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and separates.  The enumeration returns if and only if at least one such bounded candidate exists.  For a returned candidate \(p^\dagger\), denominator positivity and \(F_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq0\) give
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger),
\]
so the two intervention vectors differ.  This is incompatible with the universal equality certified by the first branch, establishing mutual exclusivity and soundness.  The argument supplies no bounded rational candidate merely from a nonzero normal form, which is why no unconditional termination claim is made.
